steps.label: Input
steps.summary: Start the run with this turn’s message and the conversation so far.
steps.use: The entry step; one is enough, and it does not wait for another message: every Input reached exposes the same request. LLM steps read the current message without one. No model call, except that history: summarize folds the oldest messages of a long server-kept conversation into a summary (one small model call each time it happens).
guide: Every run starts at the step marked entry and follows its connections. Graphs with several Input steps still work: each one reached shows the same request, not a new turn.
Long conversations: steps get the latest messages, and the oldest are left out only when a model’s context window is full. With Summarize, nothing changes while the conversation fits.

Near what the step models can take (about half of the smallest context window, at most 100k tokens), Summarize folds the oldest messages into a summary and keeps the latest word for word. Each fold is one small model call. Apps that send their own history decide what to send.

steps.label: Reply
steps.summary: End a path with the reply the reader sees, plus pictures, audio or result data for your app.
steps.use: Ends a path. text is what the reader sees (templates such as {{answer.json.reply}}). attachments adds Image or Speech URLs under it. data is the run’s result for the app or system that called the agent (a label, a score, a handoff and its reasons, a content gap): returned beside the reply, listed in run history, never shown to the reader. Passages the text cites as [n] become numbered citations; sources sets how Chat Completions lists them in the text (markdown or text), since many chat clients show only the text. No model call.
guide: Insert the reply from an earlier step, such as your LLM’s reply text, or write a fixed message. Fields are filled in when the workflow runs.
An Image step’s address is shown under the reply; a Speech step’s is played under it.

Result data is JSON your app reads as output.data (data with Chat Completions); run history lists it and readers never see it. Many chat clients show only the text, where [1] leads nowhere: choose a source list for those. Requests can override it with sources.

steps.label: Ask user
steps.summary: Reply with a question and wait. The next message in this conversation carries on from here.
steps.use: Collects a detail from the user (an email, a course) and resumes here on their next message as {{id.answer}}. Needs a server conversation; with client history or none, the question is just the reply. Outputs of earlier steps don’t carry over to the next turn: keep what you need in a State step with conversation scope. No model call.
guide: The turn ends with the question as the reply (awaiting_input is true). When the user answers in the same conversation, the workflow carries on from this step, and {{stepId.answer}} holds their answer.
Outputs from earlier steps don’t carry over to the next turn. Keep what you need with a State step that keeps values for this conversation.
Requests that send their own history, or none, have no conversation to come back to, so the question is simply the reply.

steps.label: LLM
steps.summary: Write a reply, or return named fields, with one call to a chat model.
steps.use: One model call (one more if named fields come back as invalid JSON). Best for writing an answer from material it is given, rewriting a follow-up into a standalone query, or a judgment returned as named fields (outputs) that a Branch reads. A list output returns several items with fields of their own, for an Image step’s list or a For each step. Cannot search or call tools: use an Agent step for that.
guide: Instructions say what this model does: the main task, not just a decision. Insert passages from a Knowledge step, such as {{search.context}}, to answer from your sources.

Answer format: plain text is read as {{stepId.content}}. Named fields are read one by one, such as {{stepId.json.needs_help}}, so a Branch can decide on them. A list holds several items, each with fields of its own, instead of numbered copies like prompt_1, prompt_2.
A URL in the message is just text. To show the model pictures from earlier steps, add them under Image inputs and choose a chat model that supports image input.

steps.label: Agent
steps.summary: Let a model choose tools (knowledge search, memory, web pages, other agents) until it can answer.
steps.use: A tool loop: each search, read or hand-off is one more model call (max_turns tool calls, 1–20, default 5, up to 4 at once), so it is slower and costlier than fixed steps and its path varies by question. Best for open-ended help that needs several searches, whole sections, memory, web pages or other agents. Returns text only ({{id.content}}, no named fields), so a rule that must hold every time should not rest on its instructions alone: add a check.
guide: Give clear instructions and only the tools it needs. Each tool call is one more model call; Most tool calls bounds the loop.
The final answer is {{stepId.content}}; {{stepId.tool_calls}} lists what it did. Tools run with the same limits as the matching steps.
Knowledge and agents must belong to this agent’s project. Memory needs a user identifier (user) or a server conversation.

A run lasts 60 seconds unless the agent’s run limits allow more (up to 120); background jobs get 5 minutes. Near the limit the agent answers with what it has. For careful reading (complete lists, comparisons), a model with reasoning helps more than extra calls.

steps.label: Image
steps.summary: Draw or change pictures: one prompt, or a list of them (several scenes, or one scene several times).
steps.use: One image call per description; n pictures from one description is still one call. A list (items, usually an LLM list output) draws every picture three at a time, and nothing in it stops the run: safety refusals are marked blocked (or tried once with a fallback prompt), a busy service is retried once. Pictures are remembered by number for later turns (conversation.pictures), so an item with source 2 changes picture 2. summary is a ready-made status sentence for the reply.
guide: One scene several times: one prompt with Pictures per prompt above 1 (one call). Several scenes: a list whose items each have a prompt (one call each). A list output from an LLM step, such as pictures with prompt, label and source, is the usual source.

To change an earlier picture, give its number as Picture to change (or let a list item name it). The conversation remembers every picture it showed, so later turns can say “make picture 2 night-time” without State or URLs.

The result lists each picture with its status (ready, blocked or failed), plus addresses for the reply, counts such as ready_count, and summary: a sentence such as “Picture 1 is ready.” Unfinished pictures can be drawn later from conversation.unfinished in the same numbers. Image calls are metered.

steps.label: Speech
steps.summary: Read text aloud and pass the recording’s address to later steps.
steps.use: One speech-model call; returns an audio URL for the Reply’s attachments. For young readers, language practice and accessibility. Reads plain text: Markdown, citation numbers and links are dropped, and text longer than 4,096 characters is cut at a sentence end. Placed between the answering step and the Reply, it reads the answer while it streams.
guide: Insert the answer to read, such as {{answer.content}}, into Text. Choose a voice for the main language: other languages in the answer (a Chinese explanation, an English word) are read by a matching voice.

Insert {{stepId.url}} into a Reply step’s picture or audio: chat pages and Try it play it under the reply. Put Speech between the answering step and the Reply and the text still streams. Speech is metered per audio minute.

steps.label: Transcribe
steps.summary: Turn a recording into text for later steps.
steps.use: One transcription-model call. Reads the audio file sent with the message (apps send it as a file part) or an HTTPS address, up to 25 MB; returns the transcript. steps.use: Search only, no chat model: fast and cheap. One search of 1–5 knowledge bases for the query it is given; returns passages with sources and a count. Best before an llm that must answer only from the sources. Short follow-ups (“and on Saturday?”) search better after an llm rewrites them.
guide: Insert {{stepId.context}} into an LLM’s instructions: numbered passages with titles and addresses, ready to cite as [n].

Each knowledge base searches by keywords and meaning, reranked, or by keywords alone (no AI calls), as set on the knowledge base. {{stepId.results}} holds each passage, score and source; {{stepId.count}} is 0 when nothing matched, so a Branch can handle it.

steps.label: Memory
steps.summary: Recall or keep lasting facts about the user across conversations.
steps.use: mode recall (the default) and save need no model; extract makes one model call that adds at most 5 facts and removes ones now wrong. Needs a user identifier or a server conversation, otherwise the step is skipped. For facts that should last across conversations; for this conversation only, use State.
guide: Recall returns relevant memories as {{stepId.text}}. Learn asks a model to pick lasting facts from the exchange and update the user’s memory. Save keeps one fact you write.
Memory belongs to this agent and the user: send user with each run (for example your app’s student ID). Without it, a server conversation is used; otherwise memory steps are skipped.
Review and delete stored memories in Test → Memory.

steps.label: Branch
steps.summary: Choose a path by a field from an earlier step, such as an LLM’s named field.
steps.use: Free and deterministic: branch on a field from an earlier step (an llm's structured output, a knowledge count, a guardrail or http result). One condition (expr) goes to true or false; cases are checked in order, the first that holds decides, else default. A case may have a label, shown on its connection.
guide: One condition has two paths: Yes when it holds, No when it doesn’t. Several cases are checked from the top; the first that holds decides, and Otherwise takes the rest.
Build a case from rules on earlier steps’ fields, such as “tutor → pictures has an item without a prompt”. Name it so the canvas shows what it means.
Rules that can’t be shown as rules are kept as an expression. Nothing is rewritten until you edit it.

steps.label: Loop
steps.summary: Repeat steps a number of times, or while a condition holds.
steps.use: Repeats a sub-path by count or while a condition holds. A run visits a Loop at most 25 times, so a count of 24 is the most that finishes; every pass spends its steps’ model calls and counts toward the run’s 50 steps. For one pass per item of a list, use For each.
guide: Connect continue to the first repeated step and the last repeated step back to this Loop. Connect done to the step after the loop.
The counter starts at 1. A count of 3 runs the steps three times; the fourth visit takes done. While is checked before each pass, and a count wins over it.
Outputs from repeated steps are replaced each pass, not collected. The run’s step, model call and time limits still apply.

steps.label: For each
steps.summary: Run the same steps once for every item of a list, then carry on with what each pass kept.
steps.use: Goes through a list (usually an LLM list output) one item at a time, up to max_items (default 10, at most 25): the steps from “for each item” back to this step run for every item and read it as {{item}} and {{item_number}}. Each pass spends its steps’ model calls and counts toward the run’s limits. Steps inside can’t reply or ask. For pictures, an Image step with a list is simpler.
guide: Connect “for each item” to the first step to repeat, and the last of those steps back to this one. Connect “when done” to the step after.
Steps inside read the current item as {{item}} (its fields as {{item.text}}) and its position as {{item_number}}. Give it a name, such as question, to read {{question}} instead.
After the loop, {{stepId.values}} lists what each pass kept (the last step’s result unless you choose), and {{stepId.results}} keeps every step’s output per item.

steps.label: Parallel
steps.summary: Run several paths at the same time, then carry on at the join step once all finish.
steps.use: Runs 2–6 independent paths at the same time, then continues at the join. Saves time, not model calls. If any path fails, the run fails.
guide: Connect each path to its first step, and the end of every path to the same join step. Paths must not reply on their own.
Every output from every path is there after the join, such as {{critic_a.json.feedback}} and {{critic_b.json.feedback}}.

steps.label: Fetch URL
steps.summary: Read one public HTTPS address, or send JSON to an API. It doesn’t search the web or run a site’s JavaScript.
steps.use: No model. GET reads one public HTTPS URL (10 seconds, 5 MiB download, 256 KiB after cleanup; no web search or JavaScript); POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE with a JSON body sends to an API or webhook, for example to notify staff. Needs the exact URL; never credentials. A step saved without a method sends POST, as older graphs did.
guide: Paste a full website or API address, such as https://example.com. GET reads it; headers and body can stay empty.
Returns JSON or plain text. HTML comes back as Markdown plus its links and images (address and ALT text). PDFs, images, login-only pages and pages built by JavaScript can’t be read.
POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE send a JSON body and may change data at the destination. Never put passwords, keys or tokens in a workflow: every project member can read them.
For pages your agent should always know, add them to a knowledge base instead: they are read once and refreshed on a schedule.

steps.label: Component
steps.summary: Run another team’s method as a step: a component you call with only the learner data its manifest lists.
steps.use: No model call of its own. Runs a step component (the Harness’s docs/components.md) from its manifest, pasted whole into the step: sends only the fields its receives lists, each worked out from inputs (a template per field), to its entry on a host its sends_to names, never following a redirect, 30 seconds and 1 MiB at most. It answers { output, flags }: later steps read {{id.output}} and {{id.flags}}. VIABLE calls http components only, over public HTTPS; an MCP server runs with viable-engine serve on your own machine. A refusal, timeout or answer out of shape stops the run unless on_error is continue (status failed, error).
guide: Paste or upload the component’s manifest, the JSON file its authors publish. Its slot must be step, and on VIABLE it runs over HTTPS.
For each field the component receives, choose what the run sends, such as the learner’s message or a step’s reply. A field left empty isn’t sent.
It sends only to the hosts its manifest names and never follows a redirect. Keep learners’ names and other identifiers out of what you send.
Later steps read its answer and flags. If it can’t be reached or answers out of shape, the run stops, unless you choose to keep going without it.

steps.label: VETTING
steps.summary: Have an independent reviewer check each reply against your rules, and revise it until one passes.
steps.use: Two model calls per attempt (a reply and an independent review, up to max_attempts, 1–10, default 3); one when an earlier step’s answer (draft) passes as written. For replies that must follow rules before they reach learners: tutoring that guides without giving answers away (mode full, with an answer key), and course, program or library assistants that may state only what their syllabus, catalog or guides say (a guideline with a reference). Same logic as the /v1/vetting endpoints. Exits: passed, unverified, attention.
guide: Each attempt: the reply model writes, then the reviewer model checks the reply in a separate call. A failed review goes back as feedback for the next attempt. The reviewer’s rules live in this step, apart from the reply model’s instructions, so a learner can’t talk the reviewer out of them.

A guideline checks your rules (like /v1/chat/vetting); a reference gives the reviewer material to check facts against, such as the passages an answer came from. An answer key checks a question’s answer isn’t given away (like /v1/vetting/full): a reply that confirms an answer as the learner’s own passes, and one that supplies it fails. Where code finds the learner has written the answer (a number, or a few words), both models are told they are right: the reply says so and may discuss it, and a reply that leaves them unsure fails. The reviewer reads the reply, never the learner’s words. Only the reviewer sees the reference and the answer key.

To check a reply another step wrote (an agent that answered from your knowledge, say), put it in Answer to review, such as {{research.content}}, and give the reviewer the sources as reference. A reply that passes is used exactly as written; the reply model revises it only after a failed review.

A learner waits for every round, a reply and a review, with nothing on the page until one passes. That is a choice to make: fewer Attempts or a faster Reviewer model means a shorter wait and more replies ending unverified; more means the other way. The defaults are a place to start, and Try it and Run history show how long a reply took.

Exits: passed (the reviewer approved), unverified (attempts ran out or a review couldn’t run), needs attention (the reply model flagged a safety concern and wrote a caring reply, which isn’t reviewed). Read the reply as {{stepId.content}}. A review is a model judgment, not a guarantee.

steps.label: Guardrail
steps.summary: Check text for personal data, jailbreaks, harmful content, off-topic requests or your own policy.
steps.use: pii is pattern matching with no model (emails, phone, payment card and US SSN numbers); jailbreak, moderation, off_topic and custom share one model call. Exits pass and fail. For public or student-facing input, or to screen a reply before it is sent. A model judgment, not a guarantee; for rules a reply must follow, VETTING revises instead of only failing.
guide: Personal data needs no model: emails, phone numbers, payment card and US Social Security numbers. {{stepId.redacted_text}} masks them.
Allowed topic is read only by the Off topic check, and Custom policy only by the Custom policy check. To judge follow-up questions in context, turn on earlier turns.
The other checks share one model call. Connect pass and fail to reply safely or carry on; {{stepId.flagged}} gives each finding and its reason.
A guardrail is a model judgment, not a guarantee. Put one before your main model to screen input, or after it to screen output.
